notes: The two-equation case is proved independently, avoiding the documented circular induction. However, the assertion after Theorem 1 that the system is unsolvable exactly when ψ fails is false. Take K=M=Q(t), L₁=∂, f₁=1/t, and U₁=V₁=1. Then ψ is true, but x'=1/t has no rational solution: rational derivatives cannot have simple poles. Solvability requires both ψ and solvability of the reduced equation.
